passage: Class 9 observation note. Lalremsiami has seemed on edge for three weeks. She told me, "One day Damini saves me a seat and calls me her favourite. The next day she doesn't look at me, and I don't know what I did." On Tuesday Damini asked her to remove a group photo of another girl as "proof" she was on the group's side. Lalremsiami said she felt sick about it and did not do it. I asked her what she noticed about the pattern; she said the kindness always comes back after she gives in. I did not tell her what to feel about Damini. I suggested she keep sitting with the reading club girls, who are steady, and I have arranged a time for her with the counsellor. She left looking tired but lighter.

qa.q: What did Damini ask Lalremsiami to do on Tuesday?
qa.a: She asked her to remove a group photo of another girl as proof she was on the group's side.

qa.q: What was Lalremsiami feeling about the request?
qa.a: She felt sick about it. Her worry shows in how she says she does not know what she did when the warmth is withdrawn.

qa.q: What did Lalremsiami do that showed she had noticed the pattern?
qa.a: She refused the loyalty test and said the kindness always comes back after she gives in. The teacher then pointed her toward steadier friends and the counsellor.

qa.q: How might Damini see her own behaviour?
qa.a: Perhaps she wants to feel sure of her place in the group, and the passage does not say. To Lalremsiami, though, the warmth and coldness feel like a test.

grounding: A teacher's note records a clique leader granting and withdrawing warmth to keep Lalremsiami anxious, and her refusal and steadier friendships.

passage:
In the girls' group at the kasba school, everything went through Nazia. If she smiled at you in the morning, your whole day was warm. If she didn't, nobody else would either.
Bidisha had been inside the circle for a month. Monday: Nazia shared her aam papad with her. Tuesday: nothing, not even a glance. Wednesday: arm around her shoulders. Bidisha's stomach never stopped churning.
On Friday Nazia said, "If you're really my friend, you won't talk to Rupa any more. She thinks she's clever."
Rupa sat next to Bidisha on the tempo every morning. She had shared her maths notes when Bidisha was sick.
Bidisha went home and wrote the week in her notebook. Warm, cold, warm, test. Written down, it looked like a trick.
On Saturday on the tempo, she sat beside Rupa as usual. When Nazia's cousin glared, Bidisha simply smiled back. Her heart raced, but she stayed.

qa.q: What did Nazia share with Bidisha on Monday?
How did Bidisha feel as Nazia switched from warm to cold?
qa.a: She felt anxious and on edge, her stomach churning because she never knew which Nazia she would get.

qa.q: What helped Bidisha break free of the pattern?
qa.a: Writing the week down showed her the warm-cold trick, so she refused Nazia's loyalty test and stayed with steady, kind Rupa.

qa.q: How might Rupa see Bidisha sitting beside her on Saturday?
qa.a: Rupa probably feels relieved and valued, since their friendship is steady and she had helped Bidisha before.

grounding: A teen notices a group leader's pattern of giving and withdrawing warmth, refuses a loyalty test and chooses a steady friend.

passage:
In their Singapore school, Xin decided who sat where. Bilal had been in her orbit all term. Some days she texted him first thing: "u're my favourite person." Other days she walked past him like he was air.
He spent a lot of time guessing which day it was.
Then on Friday: "My party's Saturday. If you come, you're in for real. If you go to your cousin's birthday instead, don't bother coming back."
Bilal's cousin Yasin was turning seven. He'd promised to do the magic trick.
He sat on his bed and scrolled back through the texts. Favourite person. Silence. Favourite person. Silence. It was a pattern, like a switch.
He texted back: "I'm going to Yasin's. Have fun." His hands were cold.
On Monday he sat with Arjun's table instead, the boys who talked about badminton and didn't keep score. Nobody tested him. Nobody needed to.

qa.q: What was Bilal's cousin Yasin turning?
How did Bilal feel before he texted Xin back?
qa.a: He felt anxious and cold-handed, worried about losing his place, but also clear once he saw the pattern in her texts.

qa.q: What would you advise Bilal to keep doing?
qa.a: Keep choosing people like the boys at Arjun's table who are steady and kind, and keep refusing tests of loyalty.

qa.q: How might Xin see Bilal's refusal?
qa.a: Xin may feel surprised or annoyed, since the warm-cold pattern usually kept people anxious and obedient.

grounding: A teen notices a leader granting and withdrawing warmth, refuses her loyalty test and finds steadier friends.
